methodology.overview: AFFIX-2026 scores production LLM/agent application frameworks on ten weighted dimensions (AFFIX composite) plus proprietary indices (LIE, CTI, FMC, GED, RACS, RHS, PR). Scores are EST from primary docs and named APIs as of the pin date — not marketing claims, not model quality.

dimensions.name: Abstraction Fit
dimensions.rubric90: Primitives match the job class with minimal glue; happy path and escape hatch documented; few 'use another product for the core loop' caveats.
dimensions.rubric60: Usable but misfit (chat-SDK as durable OS, optimizer as serve runtime); frequent DIY for core patterns; provider-specific leaks.

dimensions.name: Control Surface
dimensions.rubric90: First-class mid-run interrupt + durable resume; explicit state; retries/timeouts as APIs; branch/join or equivalent.
dimensions.rubric60: Tool-loop only; HITL without persistence; pause does not survive process death.

dimensions.name: Observability
dimensions.rubric90: Portable traces (OTel GenAI), token/cost hooks, eval/trajectory APIs, failed-run replay path.
dimensions.rubric60: Vendor-only UI or console logs; no span export; evals are blog posts not APIs.

dimensions.name: Type & Contract Safety
dimensions.rubric90: Structured output + tool args validated end-to-end; static types catch wiring bugs; schema repair/retry on violation.
dimensions.rubric60: dict/any pipelines; structured mode optional and fragile; validation left to the model.

dimensions.name: Ecosystem Gravity
dimensions.rubric90: Dense integrations, hiring market, example corpus; default stack in its language niche.
dimensions.rubric60: Niche or young; thin hiring/examples; gravity concentrated in one cloud.

dimensions.name: Runtime Economics
dimensions.rubric90: Streaming first-class; low orchestration tax; clear concurrency; deploy fits thin services/serverless.
dimensions.rubric60: Heavy multi-agent chatter defaults; weak streaming; orchestration dominates token cost.

dimensions.name: Migration Friction
dimensions.rubric90: Prompts/tools/graphs portable; open checkpoint or easy export; model string swap without rewrite.
dimensions.rubric60: Proprietary schemas; hosted ops required for core features; succession tax.

dimensions.name: Production Hardening
dimensions.rubric90: Documented durable execution, timeouts, auth/secrets patterns, idempotency, crash recovery.
dimensions.rubric60: Demo-grade loop; durability DIY without first-party integration; weak timeout/idempotency story.

dimensions.name: DX Velocity
dimensions.rubric90: Mid-level eng ships streamed tool-calling agent in hours; docs match reality.
dimensions.rubric60: Steep concept load; docs lag APIs; hello-agent requires platform setup.

dimensions.name: Future-Proofing
dimensions.rubric90: First-class MCP (client±server), A2A/interop, model-agnostic core, OTel-portable.
dimensions.rubric60: Single-vendor protocol surface; weak MCP/A2A; telemetry locked to one UI.

indices.name: Lock-in Entropy
indices.definition: Bits of irreversible coupling (vendor ops, proprietary checkpoints, cloud-only runtimes, succession traps). Ops gravity dominates import counts.

indices.name: Cognitive Tax Index
indices.definition: Concepts a mid-level engineer must learn before shipping a reliable tool-calling agent with eval + tracing.

indices.name: Failure-Mode Coverage
indices.definition: Coverage of 12 canonical production failure modes with first-class APIs (see FAILURE_MODE_MATRIX).

indices.name: Graph Expressiveness Density
indices.definition: Useful control-flow patterns (branch, join, map-reduce, interrupt, subgraph, checkpoint) per framework surface.

indices.name: RAG-to-Agent Continuum Score
indices.definition: Smoothness of evolution from retrieval pipeline → tool agent → multi-agent/durable without primary rewrite.

indices.name: Rewrite Hazard Score
indices.definition: EST P(outgrow primary orchestration within 12 months of production)×100 = clamp(0.28(100-RACS)+0.22(100-FMC)+0.18·CTI+0.17·max(0,DX-PH)+0.15(100-PH)).

findings.title: AFFIX leaders are not rewrite-safe
findings.body: Among frameworks with AFFIX ≥ 81, RHS does not fall monotonically with AFFIX. PydanticAI and Mastra are rewrite-safe; Vercel AI SDK ranks mid-AFFIX but high-hazard as a sole agent OS.
findings.evidence: affix_matrix.json; VS FMC 55 / PH 68 vs DX 94; PD durable execution + Logfire.
findings.falsifier: If VS production teams show ≤15% primary-stack rewrite at 12 months while PD ≥30%, claim fails.

findings.title: Highest Control Surface ≠ lowest Rewrite Hazard
findings.body: LangGraph leads CS (95) yet RHS (28.7) trails Mastra, Spring AI, and OpenAI Agents SDK. Checkpoint power does not cancel RACS gap, CTI, or DX–PH inversion.
findings.evidence: LG persistence + interrupts docs; dossier LIE 68, CTI 82, RACS 62.
findings.falsifier: If LG starters show lower 12-month rewrite than MA/PD at matched complexity, claim fails.

findings.title: Lock-in is ops gravity, not pip lines
findings.body: OpenAI Agents SDK advertises model portability but LIE=55: tracing, sessions, sandbox, and Responses defaults dominate coupling.
findings.evidence: OA models/tracing/sessions docs; multi-agent cluster insight.
findings.falsifier: Common production OA deploys with zero OpenAI-hosted ops and full feature parity → LIE overstated.

findings.title: DX surplus predicts production cliffs
findings.body: Frameworks with DX−PH ≥ 15 map to elevated RHS (VS, smolagents, CrewAI). Shipping velocity without hardening APIs is the cliff.
findings.falsifier: If DX−PH is non-significant (p>0.1) against rewrite outcomes, drop term from RHS.

findings.title: Microsoft succession tax underprices SK greenfield risk
findings.body: SK AFFIX understates greenfield cost while Agent Framework is the marketed successor. MS is the correct greenfield score.
findings.evidence: SK orchestration docs; MS migration guide from Semantic Kernel.
findings.falsifier: If Microsoft freezes SK orchestration as LTS without MAF pressure for 24 months, claim fails.

findings.title: RACS champions are not AFFIX champions
findings.body: LlamaIndex best RACS (92) with mid AFFIX — continuum excellence does not cancel LIE/CTI tax.
findings.falsifier: If LI hiring CTI measured ≤40 on the same rubric, paradox dissolves.

findings.title: Protocol-ready ≠ migration-easy
findings.body: ADK leads PR (96) via MCP+A2A+OTel while MF=52. DSPy inverts: lowest LIE, weakest PR.
findings.evidence: ADK A2A + traces; DSPy optimizer-first docs.
findings.falsifier: ≥3 public ADK graph exports to non-ADK runtimes without rewrite → MF too low.

findings.title: Topology false friends fail POCs
findings.body: OA handoff(), AG2 GroupChat, and CrewAI hierarchical process are distinct control primitives — not interchangeable for isolation/compliance.
findings.evidence: OA handoffs; CR hierarchical; AG Network docs.
findings.falsifier: Mechanical 1:1 mapping preserving HITL, history filters, and concurrency without adapters.

findings.title: Code-act security is bipolar
findings.body: First-class sandboxes concentrate in OA and smolagents; most frameworks push isolation to tool authors.
findings.falsifier: First-party sandbox primitives in LG/CR/AD comparable to E2B/Docker client APIs.

findings.title: Haystack 3 is the quiet RACS alternative
findings.body: HS RACS=85 with better LIE than LlamaIndex; Pipeline vs Agent clarity for EU/enterprise RAG shops.
findings.falsifier: If HS Agent lacks PipelineTool/MCPTool continuum at audit date, RACS overstated.

findings.title: Spring AI CTI is conditional on org DNA
findings.body: SP CTI=28 assumes Spring Boot fluency; effective CTI for Next.js engineers is much higher.
findings.falsifier: Blind CTI survey: non-JVM eng completes SP tool-agent+trace path in ≤ VS hours.

findings.title: DSPy inverts learning order
findings.body: Lowest LIE and highest RHS: optimizer-first curriculum leaves FMC/PH gaps; teams outgrow DSPy as runtime while keeping it as compiler.
findings.falsifier: ≥50% of production DSPy users run it as sole serve runtime at 12 months.

findings.title: LlamaIndex durable means DIY journal
findings.body: Official LI durable-workflow docs say there is no built-in checkpointer. Continuum excellence (RACS 92) can coexist with mid production hardening — adjudicated PH 72 / FMC 68 / RHS 27.1.
findings.evidence: https://developers.llamaindex.ai/python/llamaagents/workflows/durable_workflows/ — “There is no built-in checkpointer”; contrast LangGraph PostgresSaver.
findings.falsifier: First-party LI checkpointer that persists/resumes without a custom loop or DBOS opt-in.

findings.title: OpenAI model portability is beta; ops are not
findings.body: LiteLLM in the Agents SDK is best-effort beta while Traces default to OpenAI’s dashboard. Lock-in is an ops-default problem — LIE raised 55 → 58 after primary-source audit.
findings.evidence: openai-agents-python models (LiteLLM beta) + tracing docs (set_trace_processors required to replace OpenAI export).
findings.falsifier: GA non-OpenAI adapter + OTel-native default export with OpenAI Traces opt-in only.

findings.title: AI SDK 7 documented the agent-OS gap
findings.body: Core ToolLoopAgent stays in-memory; durable loops live in @ai-sdk/workflow. Sole-stack VS PH 65 / FMC 52 → RHS 34.5 — still high-hazard for orchestration.
findings.evidence: ai-sdk.dev WorkflowAgent vs ToolLoopAgent table; telemetry via @ai-sdk/otel; AI SDK 7 changelog.
findings.falsifier: Durable agent loop + OTel ship in core ai with crash-safe defaults.

findings.title: SK orchestration is still prerelease
findings.body: Semantic Kernel Agent Orchestration installs with --prerelease while Microsoft Agent Framework is marketed as the direct successor. Greenfield SK AFFIX understates succession tax.
findings.evidence: learn.microsoft.com SK agent-orchestration (--prerelease) + Agent Framework overview (“direct successor”) + migration guide.
findings.falsifier: SK orchestration GA without prerelease and successor language withdrawn for 24 months.

findings.title: Protocol leadership ≠ rewrite safety
findings.body: ADK leads Protocol Readiness (PR 96) via A2A + MCP + OTel, but high PR does not compress rewrite hazard the way PydanticAI’s durable typed stack does (RHS 17.3).
findings.evidence: adk.dev A2A, MCP tools/to_mcp_server, traces; pydantic.dev durable_execution.
findings.falsifier: ≥3 public case studies exporting ADK graph/session state to a non-ADK runtime without control-flow rewrite.

personas.note: Fastest streamed chat UI. Schedule Mastra/Inngest hardening by month 3 (RHS 32.9).

personas.avoid: Shipping research code as prod serve path
personas.note: Highest GED; plan OA/PD/AD serve-path before production (AG RHS 36).

personas.note: Best CS/FMC/PH; interrupt + checkpointer is the compliance default.

personas.avoid: LG JS alone for greenfield; SP
personas.note: Compose UI stream contracts with agent OS workflows/memory.

personas.alt: DS compile → PD serve; LI/HS for RAG-heavy

frameworks.name: PydanticAI
frameworks.oneLiner: Typed Python agent SDK with first-party durable engines and OTel-native observability.
frameworks.bestFor: Typed Python production agents with durable execution and OTel
frameworks.notFor: Do not pick PydanticAI when the product is a React/Next streaming UI (use VS±MA), when the bottleneck is automatic prompt search (use DSPy as compiler), or when you need LangGraph-class arbitrary mid-graph interrupts without adopting a durable engine/Harness persistence.

primitives.hitl: Deferred tool calls / approval via durable engines + Harness; AG-UI tool approval interrupts
primitives.checkpoint: StepPersistence (Harness); TemporalDurability / DBOS / Prefect / Restate / Lambda / Airflow backends
primitives.stream: agent.run stream / StreamedRunResult; AG-UI and Vercel AI UI bridges
primitives.structured: Agent(..., output_type=Model); tool/native/prompted modes; Pydantic validation + retry
primitives.obs: Instrumentation capability; logfire.instrument_pydantic_ai(); plain OTel; Pydantic Evals
primitives.multiAgent: capabilities SubAgents / multi-agent guides; Pydantic Graph for typed control flow
primitives.mcp: capabilities=[MCP(url)] client; MCP API module; Logfire MCP in Harness

frameworks.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
frameworks.oneLiner: OpenAI's agent runtime: handoffs, guardrails, HITL RunState, MCP, sandbox agents.
frameworks.bestFor: OpenAI-standardized orgs needing handoffs, guardrails, sandbox code-act
frameworks.notFor: Do not use as the sole stack if you require vendor-neutral ops (Traces/Sandbox/session gravity is real), or if you need open graph checkpoint export across non-OpenAI runtimes without adapters.

primitives.checkpoint: Sessions + RunState; Temporal/Restate integrations for durable runs
primitives.stream: Runner streaming events; results stream APIs
primitives.structured: Agent output types / structured outputs on agents
primitives.obs: Built-in tracing; exportable spans; guardrail hooks

frameworks.name: Google ADK (Agent Development Kit)
frameworks.oneLiner: Google's multi-language agent kit; protocol leader (MCP+A2A) with graph HITL nodes.
frameworks.bestFor: Multi-agent graphs with MCP+A2A and Google deploy paths
frameworks.notFor: Avoid as primary if you are not willing to accept Google-ecosystem gravity (deploy/A2A/GCP adjacency) or if you need the simplest typed Python DX — AD's CTI and MF punish small teams.

versions.notes: Multi-lang: Python/TS/Go/Java/Kotlin; HITL graphs from v2.0.0

primitives.checkpoint: Session/state + deploy runtimes; graph persistence patterns
primitives.mcp: MCP tools client; expose via A2A/MCP server patterns

frameworks.name: Mastra
frameworks.oneLiner: TypeScript agents + workflows + memory; the TS continuum bet beside AI SDK.
frameworks.bestFor: TypeScript agent OS: workflows, memory, HITL beside AI SDK UI
frameworks.notFor: Do not use Mastra for JVM estates or when you only need a chat UI without workflows/memory — AI SDK alone is enough; also avoid if you refuse any TS agent-platform opinions.

primitives.hitl: Tool approval / suspend execution on agents and workflows
primitives.stream: Agent and workflow fullStream / streaming responses
primitives.obs: Logging, tracing, eval primitives on agents
primitives.mcp: Tools invoke remote MCP servers; MCP-first agent surface

frameworks.name: LangGraph
frameworks.oneLiner: Low-level durable graph runtime; best control surface, highest cognitive tax.
frameworks.bestFor: Regulated HITL, durable graphs, time-travel debugging
frameworks.notFor: Do not start greenfield LangGraph for a simple tool loop or MVP chat — CTI and LIE are high; prefer create_agent/PD/VS until you need interrupts, time-travel, or fan-out joins.

primitives.hitl: interrupt(payload) in nodes; resume via Command
primitives.mcp: Via LangChain MCP adapters / tool nodes

frameworks.name: Vercel AI SDK
frameworks.oneLiner: Default TypeScript app-layer AI toolkit for streamed UIs and typed tools.
frameworks.bestFor: Product UI streaming chat/tools on Next.js/React
frameworks.notFor: Do not run AI SDK alone as a durable/compliance agent OS. ToolLoopAgent is in-memory; WorkflowAgent requires @ai-sdk/workflow. Weak native RAG platform and concurrent state control.

primitives.hitl: toolApproval on generateText/streamText/ToolLoopAgent; WorkflowAgent durable approval
primitives.checkpoint: WorkflowAgent (@ai-sdk/workflow) persists steps; ToolLoopAgent is in-memory
primitives.obs: telemetry API (AI SDK 7); DevTools; OTel-oriented exporters
primitives.multiAgent: ToolLoopAgent loops; handoffs via tools; not a graph OS

frameworks.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
frameworks.oneLiner: Microsoft's enterprise agent/workflow successor to Semantic Kernel orchestration.
frameworks.notFor: Do not choose MS if you are outside Microsoft/.NET/Azure estates without a migration plan; brownfield SK apps should budget succession, not pretend SK orchestration is LTS.

versions.notes: Microsoft Agent Framework; SK succession path

primitives.structured: Strong typed contracts on .NET; schema validation
primitives.mcp: MCP tool bridges in Agent Framework docs

frameworks.name: CrewAI
frameworks.oneLiner: Role-based crews and Flows with approachable multi-agent DX.
frameworks.bestFor: Fast role-based multi-agent demos and Flows
frameworks.notFor: Do not ship role-play crew demos as regulated production without Flows/checkpoints/guardrails hardening; concurrent state races are under-specified vs graphs.

primitives.mcp: MCP tool integration in recent docs

frameworks.name: LlamaIndex
frameworks.oneLiner: RAG-native data agents and workflows with the strongest continuum score.
frameworks.notFor: Avoid if you need minimal lock-in and refuse LlamaCloud/Parse gravity; also a poor fit as a pure UI streaming layer (pair with VS) or as a low-CTI toy agent.

primitives.structured: Structured outputs / Pydantic in workflows and LLMs
primitives.multiAgent: Multi-agent workflows; agent teams over documents

frameworks.name: Haystack
frameworks.oneLiner: Composable pipelines and Agent-as-Component for enterprise RAG.
frameworks.bestFor: Pipeline-first RAG/agent with lower lock-in than LlamaCloud
frameworks.notFor: Do not expect LangGraph-class crash-safe thread checkpoints; Haystack HITL is ConfirmationHook-centric. Poor fit for non-pipeline multi-actor topologies.

primitives.hitl: Human-in-the-loop ConfirmationHook on Agent tool calls
primitives.checkpoint: Pipeline state; no LG-class thread checkpointer

frameworks.name: Spring AI
frameworks.oneLiner: Spring-native AI: ChatClient, Advisors, Micrometer, MCP starters.
frameworks.notFor: Do not recommend Spring AI to Next.js/Python shops — CTI explodes without Spring Boot DNA. Not a durable graph agent runtime.

versions.notes: Milestone BOM as of pin; confirm GA before prod pin

primitives.hitl: No first-class mid-graph interrupt; app-level approval patterns
primitives.multiAgent: Advisors + tools; limited native multi-agent graph DSL

frameworks.name: LangChain
frameworks.oneLiner: High-gravity orchestration layer; v1 agents compile onto LangGraph.
frameworks.bestFor: Ecosystem gravity, LangSmith, and LC→LG funnel shops
frameworks.notFor: Do not assume 'LangChain only' avoids LangGraph lock-in once HITL/memory ship — create_agent funnels into LG persistence. High LIE for portable graphs.

primitives.checkpoint: Short-term memory / threads via LangGraph persistence
primitives.stream: Agent/graph streaming; frontend HITL stream helpers
primitives.mcp: MCP tool adapters in LangChain ecosystem

frameworks.name: AutoGen / AG2
frameworks.oneLiner: Multi-agent research topologies (GroupChat/Network) with high expressiveness.
frameworks.notFor: Do not productize research GroupChat topologies without a serve-path rewrite plan (RHS high). Classic→v1 is non-drop-in.

primitives.hitl: Human proxy agents / input requests in chat patterns
primitives.checkpoint: Partial; session/state helpers, not LG-class default
primitives.structured: Partial typed messages; weaker than PD/VS
primitives.multiAgent: GroupChat, Network, channel protocols — highest GED
primitives.mcp: MCP integrations present; less polished than AD/PD

frameworks.name: Microsoft Semantic Kernel
frameworks.oneLiner: Enterprise plugins/.NET agents under active succession to Agent Framework.
frameworks.bestFor: Brownfield SK estates only (migrate to MS)
frameworks.notFor: Do not greenfield Semantic Kernel orchestration in 2026 — Microsoft Agent Framework is the successor; SK carries succession tax.

primitives.hitl: Partial / experimental on SK agent orchestration
primitives.checkpoint: Partial; prefer MS Agent Framework workflows for durable HITL
primitives.structured: Strong .NET typing; JSON schemas on functions
primitives.mcp: MCP plugins / Agent Framework MCP path

frameworks.name: Hugging Face smolagents
frameworks.oneLiner: Tiny code-act agents with first-class sandbox backends.
frameworks.bestFor: Minimal code-act prototypes with real sandboxes
frameworks.notFor: Do not use smolagents as a sole production runtime for HITL/compliance; it is a code-act prototype vehicle with sandbox strengths and FMC gaps.

primitives.structured: Weak; code-act returns over schema contracts

frameworks.name: DSPy
frameworks.oneLiner: Programmatic LM programs and optimizers — compile, don't serve.
frameworks.notFor: Do not serve DSPy as your production agent OS. Use it to optimize prompts/metrics, then serve via PD/OA/VS/LG.

versions.notes: GEPA optimizer path; not a serve OS

primitives.structured: Signatures / typed predictors — strong compile-time contracts
primitives.obs: Partial logging; not OTel-first agent traces
primitives.multiAgent: Programs composing modules; not crew/graph OS

comparisons.title: PydanticAI vs LangGraph
comparisons.verdict: PD for typed Python production defaults; LG when compliance demands arbitrary mid-graph interrupts and time-travel.
bullets: PD wins RHS (17.3 vs 28.7) and TC; LG wins CS/FMC/PH absolute control.
LG CTI 82 is the tax; PD CTI 30 with durable engines optional.
Compose: PD agents inside durable engines ≈ LG control without LG checkpoint lock-in — EST, validate for your HITL shape.

comparisons.title: Vercel AI SDK vs Mastra
comparisons.verdict: Compose both: VS for UI streams, Mastra for workflows/memory/HITL — do not treat them as substitutes.
bullets: VS EG/DX leadership; MA RACS/FMC/RHS leadership for agent OS.
AI SDK 7 WorkflowAgent narrows the gap only if you adopt @ai-sdk/workflow.

comparisons.title: LlamaIndex vs Haystack
comparisons.verdict: LI for maximum continuum; HS when lower lock-in and Pipeline clarity matter more than LlamaCloud gravity.
bullets: Near-equal AFFIX (~78.6); LI RACS 92 vs HS 85; HS LIE 42 vs LI 58.
HS DUR weaker (ConfirmationHook vs thread checkpointer).
JVM shops should consider Spring AI instead of either.

comparisons.title: OpenAI Agents SDK vs Google ADK
comparisons.verdict: OA for OpenAI-standardized product orgs; AD when MCP+A2A protocol surface and multi-cloud graphs dominate.
bullets: AD PR 96 vs OA 81; OA better SBOX and guardrails DX.
Both carry ops/cloud gravity (OA LIE 55, AD MF 52).
Handoffs (OA) ≠ AD multi-agent trees — topology false friends apply.

comparisons.title: CrewAI vs AutoGen/AG2
comparisons.verdict: CR for productized roles/Flows; AG for research topologies — neither is a free production serve path.
bullets: AG GED 95 with RHS 36; CR lower CTI, still needs hardening.
Plan PD/OA/AD serve-path before scaling either.

comparisons.title: Semantic Kernel vs Microsoft Agent Framework
comparisons.verdict: Greenfield → MS; SK only for brownfield with an explicit migration budget.
bullets: SK orchestration marked experimental/succession path in Microsoft docs.
Succession tax is unique to the Microsoft line in this study.
